newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram to discuss taxes on Sept 10.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram to discuss taxes on Sept 10.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Friday that he would discuss the tax proposals outlined in 1996/97 (April-March) federal budget in the parliament on September 10.
"Sir, today I will not deal with tax issues (today). I will have time to discuss it on the 10th," Chidambaram told the speaker of the lower house (Lok Sabha) of the parliament.
Chidambaram said he would be discussing the "broad philosophy" of the budget in parliament on Friday.
The Finance Minister was forced to postpone his speech, eagerly awaited by stock markets, earlier this week following an uproar in parliament.
Markets were expecting Chidambaram to offer concessions to industries which have lobbied his office since he presented the blueprint of 1996/97 budget on July 22.

But members of the main opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), in an uproar over a split in the Hindu nationalist party in Gujarat state, forced repeated adjournment of both houses of parliament on Tuesday.
The proceedings were disrupted on Wednesday as well on the same issue. Parliament was closed on Thursday due to a Hindu festival holiday.

BJP lawmakers were protesting against a decision by the deputy speaker of the Gujarat assembly to recognise a breakaway faction of the right-wing party, which has been shaken by rivalries in the western state.
